title: When the Protocol Breaks
premise: Xanthe Lockridge investigates impossible accidents along the Long Route, the thread of relays connecting human-settled worlds that severed diplomatic contact two centuries ago. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct since the Severance, he traces it to a dying relay at the edge of dead space and discovers its keeper is broadcasting in his own grandmother's mother tongue — proof that someone survived the purge both sides agreed to forget. Racing corporate salvagers who want the relay's archive destroyed to protect the peace, Xanthe must choose between restoring the protocol that keeps the Route alive and honoring an inheritance of memory that could shatter it. In the end he broadcasts the truth whole, accepting exile from every world he once called home, but gaining a family of listeners on both sides of the silence.
about_author: Silas Pemberton is a former maritime radio operator turned novelist who writes about distance, signal, and the people who keep lonely stations running. He lives near a decommissioned lighthouse with his partner and an aging shortwave rig.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Investigating a cargo ship that vanished between two silent worlds, Xanthe demonstrates his uncanny knack for reading accidents like sentences. The beat establishes his competence and isolation — a man fluent in systems, illiterate in belonging.

chapters.title: Impossible Frequency
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. A distress ping arrives on a dead band, encoded in a language extinct for two centuries. Xanthe recognizes fragments his grandmother sang to him. Emotional beat: dread mixed with homesickness for a place that never existed in his lifetime.

chapters.title: The Company's Interest
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. His employer, Meridian Assurance, assigns him to 'verify' the signal — with quiet instructions to discredit it. He meets Ilsa Voss, a company archivist who seems too curious about the extinct language. Beat: suspicion wrapped in charm.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Grammar
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe, flashback-woven. Sorting his late grandmother's effects, Xanthe finds hand-copied phrasebooks labeled with relay coordinates. The inheritance theme crystallizes: she left him a map disguised as nostalgia. Beat: grief turning into purpose.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. He books passage on a tramp freighter toward dead space, lying to Meridian about his route. Ilsa boards the same ship, unconvincingly by coincidence. Beat: wary alliance; two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: The Silence Between
chapters.summary: POV freighter captain Odile Marchetti. She explains why no one runs this stretch: ships that enter dead space come back with crews who won't speak of it. Superstition and economics entwine. Beat: mounting unease as the stars thin out.

chapters.title: First Dead Relay
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. They dock at a relay that should be automated but shows signs of habitation — fresh food, a child's drawing. Someone is living inside the protocol's corpse. Beat: wonder curdling into fear of what waits ahead.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Question
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Voss. Her chapter reveals her motive: her employer wants the archive erased because it proves the Severance purges were deliberate, not mutual silence. She hasn't decided whose side she's on. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Pursuit Vector
chapters.summary: POV Odile. A Meridian salvage cruiser shadows them, demanding inspection. Odile threads a debris field to slip it, burning fuel they can't spare. Beat: adrenaline and sacrifice — the captain pays a price for passengers she's grown fond of.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Voice
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. They reach the edge relay and find its keeper: an old woman, Sefi, last speaker of the language, transmitting the distress call not for rescue but as testimony. Beat: recognition — Xanthe answers her in his grandmother's accent, and she weeps.

chapters.title: What the Archive Holds
chapters.summary: POV Sefi. The relay's core contains records of the purge fleets, names of the disappeared, and the original protocol both governments rewrote. Sefi has spent forty years preparing to send it. Beat: solemnity; history as burden.

chapters.title: The Salvagers Arrive
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The Meridian cruiser docks under false colors. Ilsa must decide whether to warn Sefi or protect her cover. She chooses warning, burning her career in one transmission. Beat: betrayal inverted into loyalty.

chapters.title: Siege of the Quiet Station
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Salvagers cut power section by section, negotiating politely while stealing the station's air. Xanthe bargains using insurance law against them — delaying, stalling, buying hours. Beat: tense chess played with words.

chapters.title: Odile's Gamble
chapters.summary: POV Odile. She takes the freighter out alone to draw the cruiser off, knowing she may not have fuel to return. Beat: heartbreak and heroism; the captain becomes the story's quiet martyr figure.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: POV Sefi. Flashbacks to the purge: how she survived by hiding inside the protocol itself, becoming a ghost in the machine. She confesses she kept transmitting partly out of fear of being forgotten. Beat: raw vulnerability; survival examined as wound.

chapters.title: Compromise Draft
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. She drafts a redacted version of the archive — enough truth to satisfy conscience, little enough to avoid war. Xanthe refuses: half-truths are how the Severance happened. Beat: ideological fracture within the found family.

chapters.title: Breach
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Salvagers storm the core. Sefi is gravely injured shielding the transmitter. Xanthe holds the relay's throat, reciting the old language over open channels so the attackers hesitate — some of them understand fragments too. Beat: climax ignition.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. With Sefi dying, Xanthe transmits the full archive across every band, unencrypted, unstoppable. The salvage cruiser receives orders to stand down as the truth propagates faster than it can be suppressed. Beat: catharsis through irrevocable act.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Sefi dies with her hand in Xanthe's, making him her heir — not of property but of language. Ilsa chooses exile alongside him rather than return to Meridian. Beat: mourning braided with continuity.

chapters.title: Odile Returns
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Running on fumes and luck, the captain limps back to find the station changed and the Route stirring — relays answering each other in the old tongue for the first time in centuries. Beat: relief, awe, reunion.

chapters.title: Exiles' Harbor
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Both governments brand them criminals; neither can touch them now without confirming the broadcast. The crew claims the relay as home, opening it to refugees of the silence. Beat: belonging forged from loss.

chapters.title: When the Protocol Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe, coda. A year later, new signals arrive daily — grief, apology, names of the missing read aloud. Xanthe teaches children the grammar his grandmother kept alive. Final beat: the protocol didn't break; it was finally told the truth.
